title: Radiators and Silence
premise: Ulyana Almeida, a bridge inspector who has spent twelve years measuring what she cannot say to her husband Tomás, is hired to assess a condemned viaduct in the interior where her mother once worked as a domestic servant. There she meets Dona Serafina, the last fluent speaker of a dying river language, who asks Ulyana to record her words before the dam floods the valley. As Ulyana transcribes, she uncovers that Serafina witnessed — and was silenced about — a fatal collapse decades ago, one covered up by the same family that now owns the dam. When Tomás arrives to bring her home, the marriage's hidden fracture and the valley's buried crime force each other into the open. In the end, Ulyana testifies at an unofficial hearing in the flooded town's church, choosing truth over safety, while Serafina dies with her language recorded but her justice only half-won — and Ulyana finally says the thing she has practiced not saying for twelve years.
about_author: Mara Hartwell is the pen name of a former civil engineer who spent eight years inspecting bridges across three continents before turning to fiction. Her work explores the quiet violence of institutions and the languages we lose to progress.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On a routine inspection of a city overpass, Ulyana measures millimeters of movement and thinks about everything she and Tomás leave unsaid at dinner. A letter arrives offering a contract: assess the condemned Viaduto do Rio Escuro before the dam closes. She accepts without telling him. Emotional beat: restless avoidance dressed as duty.

chapters.title: The Last Speaker
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Arriving in the shrinking river town, she finds the viaduct sounder than reported — and meets Dona Serafina, ninety-one, who asks her to record the last of the Yawari language before the waters rise. Ulyana hesitates; this is not her job. Emotional beat: reluctant fascination, the first crack in her professional armor.

chapters.title: Words Under Water
chapters.summary: Serafina's POV. The old woman begins teaching, but her lessons keep circling one word — kaxiru — that she refuses to translate. Through her memories we glimpse 1979: workers on the viaduct, a foreman named Duarte, a night of shouting, and a section of bridge that fell with men inside it. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through vocabulary.

chapters.title: Load-Bearing
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Worried by Ulyana's silence, Tomás follows her inland, carrying twelve years of accumulated grievances he can't yet name. He arrives unannounced and finds his wife laughing with strangers in a language he doesn't understand. Emotional beat: jealousy of a intimacy he never learned to offer.

chapters.title: The Duarte File
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Digging through municipal archives for inspection records, Ulyana finds the 1979 collapse was ruled 'act of God' — signed off by Duarte, now patriarch of the family that built the dam. Serafina finally translates kaxiru: witness. The word means both 'one who sees' and 'one who must speak.' Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ulyana confronts Duarte's grandson at the dam office; he offers her money to lose her report. That night someone burns Serafina's recordings — all but the tapes hidden inside the viaduct's hollow pier. Tomás discovers the burned tapes and realizes his wife is in danger. Emotional beat: fear replacing caution.

chapters.title: Almost Saying It
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tomás's POV, split scene. Trapped together during a storm, they finally have the fight twelve years deferred — about a stillbirth, about blame, about who got to grieve out loud. Neither wins, but something unlocks. Meanwhile Serafina's health fails. Emotional beat: painful, necessary honesty.

chapters.title: The Pier
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With the flood date moved up, Ulyana rappels into the viaduct pier to retrieve the surviving tapes — and finds evidence Duarte's crew welded over structural cracks days before the collapse. Duarte's men arrive; Tomás creates a diversion that nearly kills him. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Kaxiru
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. In the half-abandoned church above the future waterline, Ulyana convenes an unofficial hearing: survivors' families, a journalist, the tapes played aloud. Serafina, carried in on a chair, gives her testimony in Yawari, translated word by word by Ulyana — her first public act of speech in the language. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Residual Stress
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, months later. The dam opens; the valley floods; the tapes reach a federal prosecutor too late for trial but not for the record. Serafina died two weeks after the hearing, her language preserved in four hundred hours of audio. Ulyana stands on a new bridge, tells Tomás she wants to try again, and signs her report with the truth intact. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
